title: Mitosis core re-spec (new SPEC, zero dependency on 2026-07-30)

completion_criteria.text: Scope modifications for the new SPEC are decided with the user and recorded as a decision record.
Brainstorming run in a FRESH session via superpowers:brainstorming before any SPEC drafting begins.
SPEC A (config staging/live promotion) authored standalone - no inherited decision numbers, no step-N chain, no citation of the 2026-07-30 document as authority.
User reviews SPEC A and approves it, before any SPEC B drafting begins.
SPEC B (mitosis core: token/latency cost, codegen decomposition, stacked PRs) authored standalone, with the fix pipeline excluded and no citation of the 2026-07-30 document as authority.
User reviews SPEC B and approves it.

closure_statement: Both SPECs were authored standalone from re-derived ground truth and approved by the user: SPEC A for config staging/live promotion and SPEC B for mitosis core cost, decomposition and stacked PRs, with the fix pipeline excluded and no citation authority inherited from the 2026-07-30 document.

spine.active_goal: Complete. Both SPECs authored standalone and approved; implementation moves to the successor thread.
spine.next_step: None on this thread - it is complete. SPEC A implementation continues on the successor thread per 0274: a fresh session dispatches a dedicated small dynamic workflow to fully implement and ship SPEC A, parallelizing its five section-7 preconditions and running the cutover serially and alone, with stacked PRs opened manually via pr.mjs pr-create --base <parent-branch> where changes block each other.
spine.last_session: Authored, self-reviewed and committed SPEC B; the user approved it, closing c5 and c6. Re-derivation falsified five citations and the self-review caught two defects in the draft.

open_risks.text: Instrument per-dispatch context before trusting any collapse win — the 2026-07-30 plan counts dispatches and wall-clock only, so Decompose fusion, Ship 13-to-1, and per-MSP reviews would all score as wins even if cost rose.

Re-derive every line citation from the current tree — mitosis.js is 5,515 lines against the cited 4,851, the phase-parity gate appears already landed, and mitosis-git.mjs moved to .claude/lib/git/pr.mjs.
Decide telemetry before making any cost claim — no token or tool-call accounting exists anywhere in the engine, so every re-exploration claim is unmeasurable today.

Do not re-run the three investigations — the engine map, stacked-PR research and config inventory cost roughly 340k subagent tokens, their transcripts are gone, and two ledger session events are the only remaining copy.

Every cost claim SPEC B makes is unmeasurable today — the engine carries no token or tool-call accounting anywhere, so a target written as a budget rather than as a falsifiable hypothesis cannot be checked against anything.
Re-derive every line citation before reusing one — mitosis.js measured 5,515 lines against the old document's cited 4,851, and mitosis-git.mjs has since moved to .claude/lib/git/pr.mjs.
parallel-plan-execution.js is dead code — its top-level dynamic imports cannot execute in the Workflow runtime, so any SPEC B design routing work through it builds on a broken entry point.

The Workflow validator is a source-level check — it rejected a script merely for containing the identifiers Date and Math.random inside typeof expressions, so generated engine output must avoid those identifiers textually.

key_decisions.title: Dependent MSP chains merge with merge-commit; standalone PRs keep squash
Workflow runtime forbids dynamic import, so codegen is the only path off the twinning tax
Split the re-spec into two specs, config promotion landing before the mitosis core
Config promotion is an immutable release subtree plus an atomic pointer rename, with live pinned to main
settings.json is excluded from releases and reconciled by an ownership manifest, with the leak gate on capture only
SPEC B is authored next in a fresh session, SPEC A is implemented before SPEC B, and SPEC B leads with the cost instrument
SPEC A is implemented and shipped by a dedicated small dynamic workflow, with stacked PRs for blocking changes

out_of_scope: Implementing any MSP from either SPEC
Editing mitosis.js, the parallel engine, or any live config path while a SPEC is being authored
The fix pipeline, which the user excluded from both SPECs and may brainstorm later as its own thread
